title: Synthesis of Graphene-Hydroxyapatite Nanocomposites for Potential Use in Bone Tissue Engineering
protocol: Synthesize pristine nHAP using 50 mL reaction mixture containing 1 M Ca(NO3)2·4H2O and 0.67 M (NH4)H2PO4.
Add NH4OH dropwise to maintain pH around 10.
Agitate the reaction mixture by ultrasound irradiation for 30 min at 500 W power and 20 kHz frequency.
Allow the solution to mature for 120 h at room temperature until precipitate settles out.
Recover nHAP by centrifugation at 1398 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Wash the precipitate with deionized water 3 times.
Lyophilize the precipitate for 48 hours.
Store dry powder at 4 °C.
Dissolve 5 mg of GNRs in a mixture of 1 M calcium nitrate tetrahydrate and 0.67 M diammonium hydrogen phosphate to a final volume of 50 mL.
Add NH4OH dropwise during the reaction to maintain pH around 10.
Agitate the resulting mixture by ultrasound irradiation for 30 min at 500 W power and 20 kHz frequency.
Suspend commercially available nHAP at a concentration of 5 mg/mL in 50 mL of DI water supplemented with 5 mg of GNRs.
Agitate the resulting mixture by ultrasonic irradiation for 30 min.
Leave the mixture undisturbed for 120 h at room temperature until maturation.
Recover the white precipitate of the resulting GNR/nHAP by centrifugation at 1398 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Wash the sample 3 times using DI water.
Lyophilize the washed sample for 48 h.
Store the dry powder at 4 °C for further use.
Perform Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy for neat samples at wavenumbers of 500-4000 cm−1.
Conduct powder X-ray diffraction analysis using an X-ray wavelength of 1.5406 Å and current and voltage settings of 40 mA and 40 kV, respectively.
Analyze the samples with 2θ ranging from 20° to 90° for powder XRD.
Evaluate the percent loading of GNR in the nanocomposite using thermogravimetric analysis.
Heat the samples from room temperature to 1000 °C at a rate of 10 °C/min under nitrogen flow during TGA.
